excerpt: Theorem~\ref{thm:decay} shows $\abs{\E e^{itQ}}^2\le(\sqrt2\,\pi e)^\ell(\ell^\ell/\ell!)^{1/2}E_\ell(M)^{-1/2}\abs t^{-\ell}$ for every $\ell\ge1$ with $E_\ell(M)>0$ and every $t\ne0$, uniformly in the rest of $A$, in $b$, $c$ and in the laws of the $X_i$; for $\ell=3$ Fourier inversion bounds the density. Proposition~\ref{prop:signs} supplies the crossing volume. For a diagonal matrix $D$ of random signs, $A-DAD$ is twice the off-diagonal block part of $A$ for the partition defined by the signs, and that part has the singular values of $A_{I,J}$, each twice. Compressed to $2m-1$ eigenvectors of $A$, the identity leaves the diagonal matrix of their eigenvalues, perturbed by an error whose mean square over the signs is small; so $2m-1$ eigenvalues give $m$ singular values of one block, and five give three.

excerpt: Banks, Garza Vargas, Kulkarni and Srivastava \cite[Theorem~2.1]{BGKS} bound densities of bilinear forms $\mathbf X^T Z\mathbf Y+\mathbf X^TU+V^T\mathbf Y+W$ in independent random matrices with bounded entry densities; for symmetric $A$ the blocks $A_{I,I}$ and $A_{J,J}$ add quadratic terms, which Section~\ref{sec:decay} tolerates. For linear forms, $a\cdot X$ with $\abs a=1$ has density at most $\sqrt2\,K$ by Rogozin's inequality \cite{Rogozin} and Ball's bound for cube sections \cite{Ball}; projections of higher rank are treated in \cite{RV,LPP}. The geometric Brascamp--Lieb inequality is due to Ball \cite{Ball} and Barthe \cite{Barthe}, and the heat-flow proof of Section~\ref{sec:proj} follows \cite{CLL,BCCT}. Small-ball bounds for polynomials go back to Carbery and Wright \cite{CW}, Costello, Tao and Vu \cite{CTV} treat quadratic forms in discrete variables, and the random sign step is the basic move of decoupling \cite{DG}.

excerpt: Let $U$ and $V$ be independent random elements of measurable spaces $\mathcal U$ and $\mathcal V$, let $h:\mathcal U\times\mathcal V\to\R$ be measurable, and let $g:\R\times\mathcal V\to[0,\infty]$ be measurable. Suppose that for almost every $v$ with respect to the law of $V$, $\PP(h(U,v)\in B)\le\int_Bg(z,v)\dd z$ for every Borel set $B$. Then $Q=h(U,V)$ has a density $p_Q$ with $p_Q(z)\le\E g(z,V)$ for almost every $z$, and $\E k(Q)\le\int_\R k(z)\,\E g(z,V)\dd z$ for every Borel $k\ge0$.

excerpt: The number five is used only in the case without pivots, through Proposition~\ref{prop:signs} with $m=3$; the diagonal pivot uses four large eigenvalues of $A$ and the pair cases use three. Four eigenvalues without pivots need not give a third large singular value in any off-diagonal block. Let $N>256$, let $w\in\R^N$ have all entries equal to $N^{-1/2}$, and let $A$ be the direct sum of two copies of the $(N+1)\times(N+1)$ matrix $\begin{pmatrix}0&w^T\\w&0\end{pmatrix}$. Its nonzero eigenvalues are $1,1,-1,-1$, its diagonal vanishes and every principal $2\times2$ minor has modulus at most $1/N<\zeta$, so $A$ has no pivot. For every partition $[n]=I\sqcup J$ the part of each copy in $A_{I,J}$ lies in a single row or a single column, namely that of the centre of the copy, so $A_{I,J}$ has rank at most two and $E_3(A_{I,J})=0$.
